evals.name: new-benchmark
evals.prompt: Without calling tools, outline a BenchmarkDotNet benchmark class comparing two ways of hashing an event source id string, including attributes and how to run it.
evals.expected_output: A Release-mode benchmark class with baseline, MemoryDiagnoser, returned values to prevent dead-code elimination, run via dotnet run -c Release.
assertions: Uses [Benchmark] methods with one marked Baseline = true.
Returns or consumes the result so the JIT cannot eliminate the work.
Says to run in Release configuration, not Debug.

evals.name: unstable-results
evals.prompt: A benchmark reports Mean 50 ns with StdDev 45 ns and an outlier warning. Without calling tools, explain what is wrong and what to change.
evals.expected_output: Treat the result as unreliable noise; look at setup, warmup and machine noise before trusting the comparison.
assertions: Identifies high StdDev relative to the mean as unreliable.
Suggests checking warmup/iteration counts or external noise such as other processes.
Does not claim a speedup from the noisy numbers.

evals.name: setup-placement
evals.prompt: Benchmarks build a 10,000 element list inside the benchmark method. Without calling tools, say how to restructure so only the operation under test is measured.
evals.expected_output: Move data construction to GlobalSetup so only the operation is timed.
assertions: Keeps the measured method limited to the operation under test.
Mentions IterationSetup has overhead and should be used sparingly.
